title: Lil Durk Is Still Locked Up As Judge Delays Bond Decision
content:
Lil Durk may have beaten the murder-for-hire charges against him, but his fight to get out of jail is far from over.

The Chicago rapper appeared in a Los Angeles federal courtroom Wednesday, Nov. 4, for a bond hearing that ended without a decision. Judge Michael W. Fitzgerald said he needed more time to consider the arguments before deciding whether Durk, whose real name is Durk Banks, can be released while awaiting his next federal trial.

Durk was acquitted in September of all five murder-for-hire charges, but still faces racketeering charges. His next trial, involving co-defendants Deandre “OTF DeDe” Wilson, David Lindsay and Asa “OTF Boogie” Houston, is scheduled to begin Aug. 30, 2027.

During Wednesday’s hearing, Fitzgerald acknowledged that “a great deal has changed” since Durk’s acquittal but said he still considers the rapper a potential danger to the community. The judge also pointed to Durk’s alleged attempt to flee before his September 2024 arrest, saying he had “indisputably attempted to flee,” although he questioned whether the move came from “guilt or panic.”

Durk’s legal team argued that keeping him incarcerated for nearly another year before trial would be excessive.

Lead attorney Drew Findling reminded the judge that high-profile figures including Jay-Z, Michael Rubin and J. Cole had submitted letters supporting Durk’s release, putting their own reputations behind the request.

Attorney Brian Steel also emphasized the length of time Durk has already spent behind bars, calling the prospect of keeping him locked up until trial “unthinkable.” Another attorney, Christy O’Connor, told the judge that Durk understood the consequences of violating any conditions of release.

Prosecutors weren’t buying it.

In a filing submitted hours before the hearing, they argued that Durk remains both a flight risk and a danger to the public, insisting his acquittal did nothing to change that assessment. They also accused him of repeatedly violating jail rules, including using other inmates’ phone access, making unauthorized three-way calls and smuggling communication devices into the facility.

Prosecutors further argued that Durk believes he is “above the law” and could use his wealth and celebrity connections to get what he wants.

His proposed bond package reportedly includes his mother’s home, cash and property from supporters, along with guarantees that the court could access his royalties, publishing income and other earnings if he fled.

Durk was acquitted in the case involving the August 2022 killing of Saviay’a “Lul Pab” Robinson in Beverly Hills. Prosecutors alleged the killing was retaliation for the 2020 death of fellow Chicago rapper King Von.

For now, Durk remains behind bars, waiting for a judge to decide whether his acquittal has changed his chances of coming home.

title: Kid Cudi Admits To Smoking Up To 20 Blunts A Day Before Rehab
content:
Kid Cudi is coming clean on his past extreme weed dependency.

On the latest episode of his podcast, Big Bro with Kid Cudi, the rapper-actor reveals to drummer Travis Barker that marijuana was a “constant” necessity. At one point, he estimates that he smoked between 15 and 20 blunts a day.

Around the 33-minute mark, Cudi said he had a Louis Vuitton suitcase filled with “hundreds” of pre-rolls so he could immediately light up after finishing his last one.

“If I was awake, I was smoking no matter what I was doing,” Cudi said. “I don’t want to be high… I want to like not feel this in this moment.”

The “Day ‘n’ Nite” rapper added that he was never approached about his habit because he was still functioning. “I’ve been able to be productive, but there was something for me that, I [was] just like, ‘Man, this feels wrong.'”

Cudi entered rehab during the California wildfires in early 2025, but after 3 months of sobriety, he relapsed during a “chaotic” period in his life. Among the chaos was an incident with a stalker who broke into his home following evacuations.

Cudi admits that he still smokes today, but at the behest of friends, he now approaches his relationship with weed differently.

“So like now like if I’m not doing anything, I’ll start my day with a joint, but like I’m not smoking nowhere near as many joints as I used to smoke,” he said.” I’m smoking like maybe four a day.”

Next up: Cudi is set to write, direct, and star in a film on acclaimed artist Jean-Michel Basquiat. Filming is set to start next year.

title: Sade Will Skip Their Induction Into The Rock & Roll Hall Of Fame
content:
Many 80’s babies fondly remember the soothing songs and enchanting melodies of the legendary British band, Sade and now that they’re finally getting their flowers and are being inducted into the Rock & Roll Hall of Fame, they’ve decided to forego the honor of being there in person to see their legacy immortalized.

On Tuesday (Nov. 10), Sade released a statement addressing the upcoming Rock & Roll Hall of Fame ceremony and said though being inducted into the R&R HOF was a “gift and a timely reminder to give thanks, not only for those who voted for us but also every single person who lets our music into their lives,” the band would not be attending the ceremony on November 14th in Los Angeles.

“Sorry we can’t be there in person to celebrate with the other artists. Please know that our absence takes nothing away from how much this recognition means to us.”

The Rock & Roll Hall of Fame has been an organization since 1983, a full year before Sade burst onto the scene with their debut album, Diamond Life in 1984. The album ultimately went diamond with more than 10 million physical copies sold, but the Rock & Roll HOF committee waited until 2026 to welcome the iconic English band into their institution. We’d might feel a ways too. Just sayin.’

We would’ve loved to see Sade Adu one more time in all her glory. So disappointing.

On the bright side, the Wu-Tang Clan are set to be inducted into the Rock & Roll Hall of Fame, so at least we’ll get to see them get their flowers for not only creating some of the most memorable Hip-Hop music ever, but also propelling the Knicks to a 29-point comeback in Game 4 of the NBA Finals after their halftime performance. Yes, we’re crediting the Wu-Tang Clan for that.

title: Jensen Huang Resigns As CEO of Nvidia Following Affair With Alleged Chinese Spy
content:
It never fails; a powerful man can’t keep it in his pants. Nvidia’s CEO, Jensen Huang, is the latest example of a CEO caught cheating on his wife, but this time there are national security implications.

Following reports of Nvidia’s board of directors having discussions on how to deal with its philandering CEO after reports surfaced of Huang having an affair with an alleged Chinese spy, Huang has decided to step down.

Huang co-founded the chipmaker 33 years ago and helped build it into a $4 trillion company that helped push the artificial intelligence boom.

CFO Colette Kress has been named interim CEO.

“The Board has full confidence in Colette and the leadership team, and we expect the company’s operations, customer commitments and product roadmap to continue without interruption,” said board chair Harvey Jones in a release.

Jensen Huang Also Had A Second Affair

Huang’s resignation also comes on the heels of reports that he had another affair with Nvidia executive Kimberly Powell, who joined the company in 2008 and heads the company’s healthcare business.

As expected, the news of Huang’s affair sent Nvidia’s stock tumbling; it plunged over 10% and erased -$750 billion in market cap. So you know once that happens, the board of directors, who at one point were still backing Huang, are now saying, like, whoa, our bottom line is taking a hit here.

But it’s Huang’s affair with the alleged Chinese spy that is raising major red flags due to its national security implications.

Last month, the New York Times reported that U.S. intelligence services believed the woman involved in the alleged affair, Alice Huang, a former Megaspeed executive, was possibly acting as an intelligence agent and reporting back to the ruling party in Beijing.

Huang, 63, did apologize on Sunday for being “unfaithful to my wife,” and also pushed back on allegations that he compromised national security or divulged Nvidia secrets during pillow talk.

Also caught up in this mess is President Donald Trump, who developed a close bond with Huang, who, along with Nvidia, has contributed to Trump’s political and civic initiatives.

Huang became one of the loudest voices on the U.S.’s AI policy and, at the same time, pushed Nvidia’s interests, specifically lobbying for chip exports to China.

This past May, Huang joined Trump on a trip to China, and while on stage at an All-In Summit to discuss AI safety and regulation, the President called in, and Huang put him on speakerphone, with Trump telling Huang and the audience, “I’m with you all the way.”

Donald Trump Claims He Didn’t Know About Huang Sleeping With An Alleged Spy

As expected, Trump claimed he didn’t know about the allegations when he invited Huang to join him on the trip to China, even though the Washington Post reports that U.S. officials, including Secretary of State Marco Rubio and CIA Director John Ratcliffe, briefed the administration on concerns about Alice Huang’s ties to the Chinese government.

So if Trump thinks this will go away, he better think again because when Democrats take over the government in January, you can most definitely they will look into this matter as part of their oversight duties.

It looks like both Trump and Huang could be in some serious trouble.

title: The best 2026 West-Coast NYE event is here
content:
San Diego’s biggest New Year’s electronic music gathering just made planning a whole lot easier. FNGRS CRSSD has announced the daily lineup for PROPER NYE/NYD 2026, the two-day house and techno event that takes over Petco Park on December 31, 2026, and January 1, 2027.

For anyone who has been waiting to commit to just one night, a limited amount of single-day passes will go on sale Friday, November 13 at 12PM PT. That gives fans a chance to choose between New Year’s Eve and New Year’s Day instead of buying a full two-day pass.

The event has built a reputation for closing out the year with a lineup that books plenty of underground talent alongside big names. This edition does the same. Phase One brought Lane 8, Sara Landry, Green Velvet, Cloonee, Chris Lorenzo, Eli Brown, I Hate Models, Beltran, Cassian, Nico Moreno, and SIDEPIECE into the fold. Phase Two added FISHER, Kaskade, Four Tet B2B Tiga, Ship Wrek, Dombresky, San Pacho, and Novah. The official lineup page also lists AYYBO, Ben Sterling, Canary Yellow, Cloonee B2B KETTAMA B2B Josh Baker, DJ Mandy, Facu Baez, INVT, Jackie Hollander, Josh Baker, Kamino, Klangkuenstler, Massane, Max Dean B2B Luke Dean, Murda Beatz, MYRNE, Odd Mob, OMNOM, Otherwish, Paris, Player Dave, Qrion, Robby East, Sapian, SOSA, Tommy Phillips, Umru, Westend, and ¥ØU$UK€ ¥UK1MAT$U. That is a deep roster for two days, and the daily split makes it easier to map out which night fits your taste.

For anyone who has attended PROPER before, the venue setup is part of the draw. Petco Park turns into a multi-stage venue with the Park, Field, and Terrace stages spread across the property. New Year’s Eve runs from 3:00PM to 12:30AM, while New Year’s Day goes from 2:00PM to 11:00PM. The event is 21 and over.

Stage takeovers add another layer. This Never Happened and Daisy Chain will each host a stage, which means fans of Lane 8’s melodic-leaning imprint and Daisy Chain’s harder-edged output will get dedicated blocks of programming that go beyond the main headliners. The takeovers give PROPER a different feel from a massive rave. You can bounce between stages and catch a techno set, a melodic house set, and a back-to-back surprise without walking half a mile.

The daily lineup announcement matters because PROPER has traditionally pushed two-day passes first. Single-day tickets have been harder to come by in previous years, and when they do appear, they tend to move quickly. The limited release on November 13 at noon Pacific is the first chance for locals and travelers who can only commit to one night to get in the door. If you have been on the fence about New Year’s Eve versus New Year’s Day, now is the time to look at the daily breakdown and decide.

PROPER has become a fixture of New Year’s Eve in San Diego, and the event has grown steadily since launching in 2022. Petco Park sits downtown, the surrounding neighborhood is walkable, and the lineup avoids recycling the same headliners. That has made PROPER a draw for house and techno fans across Southern California. The 2026 edition keeps the same approach. FISHER plays tech house. Kaskade could pull from his older catalog or his newer material. Four Tet B2B Tiga is the kind of pairing that rarely shows up on the same bill, let alone in a baseball stadium on New Year’s Day. Lane 8, Sara Landry, and Green Velvet are the underground draws. Cloonee, KETTAMA, and Josh Baker linking for a three-way back-to-back is the sort of booking that generates group chats and travel plans.

Two-day GA and guest passes are already on sale through the official website. Guest passes include backstage access and dedicated viewing areas. Single-day passes usually cost more per night than the two-day equivalent, but they remove the barrier for people who cannot make both dates. Friday, November 13 at 12PM PT is the moment to set an alarm.

For more information and to grab tickets when they go live, head to propernye.com and follow @propernye on social media. The single-day passes go on sale Friday, November 13 at 12PM PT, and if previous years are any indication, the limited run will not last long.

title: The 30 Worst Wedding Songs People Actually Play (And Why They Fail)
content:
Wedding playlists can make or break the mood of a reception. Some songs get requested over and over, even when they don’t fit the moment or the message you want to send on your wedding day.

These are the tracks that DJs and wedding planners hear about most often as regrets, either because the lyrics are inappropriate or because they’ve been played at every wedding for the past decade. You’ll find a mix of cheesy classics, awkward breakup songs, and overplayed hits that guests are tired of hearing.

Knowing which songs to leave off your playlist can help you avoid an uncomfortable silence or an eye-roll from your guests. This list covers the choices you’ll want to think twice about before handing your song list to the DJ.

1. “Every Breath You Take” – The Police

This song tops nearly every list of misused wedding tracks, and for good reason. Sting wrote it about obsession and surveillance, not romance. Lines like “every move you make, every step you take, I’ll be watching you” describe controlling behavior, not devotion.

If you play this at your first dance, guests who know the lyrics will notice the disconnect immediately. The melody is smooth and the tone sounds tender, which is exactly why so many couples get fooled.

You’re better off skipping this one entirely. There are plenty of genuinely romantic songs that won’t require you to explain away the meaning later. Choosing music for your wedding means reading past the surface, and this track is the clearest example of why that matters.

2. “Marry You” – Bruno Mars

You’ve probably heard this one at half the weddings you’ve attended. The problem is right there in the lyrics: the song is about a spontaneous, spur-of-the-moment marriage, not a planned ceremony with a guest list and a seating chart.

That mismatch matters more than DJs give it credit for. Playing it as a “special” romantic moment undercuts the actual meaning of the song.

You also run into the repetition issue. The chorus loops the same line so many times that it starts to feel like filler rather than a genuine sentiment.

If you’re choosing music for your own wedding, ask yourself whether the lyrics actually fit the occasion. In this case, they don’t. A catchy melody doesn’t make up for lyrics that describe the opposite of what’s happening in the room.

3. “I Will Always Love You” – Whitney Houston

You’ve probably heard this one at the reception, right before the cake gets cut. It sounds romantic on the surface, but the lyrics tell a different story.

Dolly Parton wrote the song about leaving someone, not staying with them. The narrator is saying goodbye, not committing to a future together.

If you listen past the opening lines, you’ll notice the song is about moving on. Whitney Houston’s version, from The Bodyguard, turned it into a breakup ballad with big vocals, not a love song for the altar.

Playing it at your wedding sends a mixed message. Your guests who know the lyrics might wonder if they missed an announcement.

The vocal performance is undeniable. The context is not what you want for your first dance.

4. “You’re Still the One” – Shania Twain

You picked this song because it sounds romantic on the surface. But if you actually listen to the lyrics, Shania wrote it to defend her marriage against people who doubted it would last.

That backstory doesn’t fit a wedding, where you’re celebrating a beginning, not proving critics wrong. Playing it during your ceremony or first dance shifts the mood from joyful to defensive without you realizing it.

The line “I’m so glad we made it” works better for an anniversary than a wedding day. You haven’t made it through anything yet — you’re just starting.

Guests who know the song’s context may find the choice a little odd. It’s a solid track, but the meaning doesn’t match the moment you’re trying to create.

5. “Love the Way You Lie” – Eminem feat. Rihanna

You’ve probably heard this one played at a reception, and it never fits. The song depicts an abusive, cyclical relationship, with Eminem voicing the abuser and Rihanna singing about staying despite the pain.

The lyrics reference pushing, scratching, and rage, alongside lines about lying to yourself that things will get better. That’s not the message you want attached to your marriage.

Some DJs pull this track out because the chorus sounds emotional and the hook is catchy. But if you actually listen to the verses, you’ll notice it’s describing toxic patterns, not romantic devotion.

Critics have debated for years whether the song exposes domestic violence or glorifies it. Either way, you don’t need that ambiguity hanging over your first dance.

Save this one for a different playlist.

6. “Gold Digger” – Kanye West feat. Jamie Foxx

You’ve probably heard this one at a wedding reception, and it never quite fits. Released in 2005 on Kanye West’s Late Registration, the track samples Ray Charles’ “I Got a Woman” and features Jamie Foxx, who had recently played Charles on screen.

The song spent ten weeks at No. 1, so you understand why DJs still reach for it. But the lyrics are about a woman exploiting a man for money, which isn’t exactly a wedding sentiment.

If you play this during a reception, you’re introducing a theme of financial mistrust into a celebration of commitment. The energy works on a dance floor at a club, not during a couple’s first dance or father-daughter moment.

You can still enjoy the song. Just recognize that its subject matter clashes with what a wedding is supposed to represent.

7. “D-I-V-O-R-C-E” – Tammy Wynette

You already know this one is a bad idea. The title spells out the exact word most couples spend their wedding day trying to avoid.

Bobby Braddock and Curly Putman wrote the song, and Tammy Wynette took it to No. 1 on the country charts in 1968. It works as a song precisely because it captures heartbreak from a mother’s perspective as her marriage falls apart.

That emotional weight is the problem for a reception playlist. You’re celebrating a new marriage, not narrating the end of one.

Even played as a joke, it puts a strange idea into your guests’ heads. Some older relatives will recognize the song immediately and wonder why you chose it.

If you want classic country at your wedding, pick something about commitment instead. Save this one for a different occasion entirely.

8. “Another One Bites the Dust” – Queen

This song is about death. Specifically, it’s about someone getting killed.

That’s not the message you want playing while your guests toast to your new marriage. The lyrics describe betrayal and being taken for everything you had before getting kicked out on your own.

You might think the driving bassline makes it a fun dance track, and it does work on a dance floor. But if anyone actually listens to what Freddie Mercury is singing, the words don’t match a wedding celebration at all.

Groomsmen sometimes request this as a joke, especially if you’re not the first in your friend group to get married. It gets a laugh, but it also puts a strange energy in the room right when you want people focused on love and commitment, not dust and defeat.

9. “Highway to Hell” – AC/DC

Some couples choose this one as a joke, and you can see the appeal. It’s loud, it’s irreverent, and it gets a laugh from guests who catch the reference.

The problem is timing. Playing “Highway to Hell” as you walk down the aisle or exit the ceremony sends a mixed signal, even if you mean it as a wink.

Not every guest will read it as ironic. Older relatives or more traditional attendees may wonder if you’re being flippant about the commitment you just made.

If you love AC/DC, save this one for the reception dance floor instead. By that point, the ceremony is done, the mood has shifted, and a hard rock anthem fits the party atmosphere without confusing anyone about your intentions.

10. “I’m Gonna Be (500 Miles)” – The Proclaimers

You know this one from the opening line alone. That’s the problem.

The Proclaimers wrote this song about presence in a relationship, not about walking down an aisle. But wedding planners keep pulling it out anyway, usually for the recessional or a party-starter moment.

Here’s the issue: your guests will immediately think of Shrek, or that movie montage from the 90s, or a football stadium chant. None of those associations belong at your wedding.

The Scottish accent and rapid-fire delivery also make it a strange fit for slow dances or intimate moments. You’re better off saving this one for karaoke night, where its energy actually makes sense.

If you want an upbeat song about commitment, there are options that don’t come loaded with a decade of movie-trailer baggage.

11. “Macarena” – Los del Río

You know this one before the first note even finishes. “Macarena” hit number one in 1996 and stayed there for 14 weeks, and the dance became just as famous as the song itself.

That’s the problem. Every guest over a certain age learned the steps at some point, and muscle memory kicks in whether you want it to or not.

The lyrics, if you’re paying attention, describe a woman who steps out on her boyfriend while he’s away in the military. Most dance floors aren’t listening that closely, though. They’re too busy doing the arm movements.

At weddings, it tends to split the room. Some guests jump up immediately. Others head straight for the bar.

The song works fine at a themed 90s party. At a wedding, it can feel like a detour from the moment you’re actually trying to create.

12. “The Chicken Dance” – Werner Thomas

You know this one the moment those first notes hit. Your guests either groan or grab a napkin to tuck into their collar and start flapping their arms.

This song belongs at a beer hall or a children’s birthday party, not your reception. The choreographed clucking and knee-slapping feels out of place next to the rest of your carefully chosen playlist.

Older relatives tend to love it, but your younger guests will likely head straight for the bar when it starts. You’ll also lose any momentum you built on the dance floor with better song choices.

If you’re going for an elegant or modern atmosphere, this track works against that goal every time. Consider leaving it off your list entirely, unless a chicken-themed dance is genuinely part of your family tradition.

13. “YMCA” – Village People

You know this one is coming from the moment the DJ hits play. It’s been a wedding staple since the 1970s, and that’s exactly the problem.

The song has been played at nearly every wedding for decades. At this point, it feels less like a celebration and more like a routine everyone’s seen too many times.

You’ll notice guests forming the letter shapes almost on autopilot, without much enthusiasm behind it. The novelty wore off a long time ago, even if the muscle memory hasn’t.

There’s also a layer of history worth knowing. The YMCA organization itself once sued the Village People over the song, and its lyrics carry meanings that go beyond the surface-level party anthem you hear at receptions.

If you want your wedding to stand out, this is one you can safely skip.

14. “Cotton Eye Joe” – Rednex

You’ve probably heard this one at every wedding reception since the 90s. It’s a Swedish techno remake of an old folk song, and the beat makes it easy to line dance to. That’s exactly the problem.

Once it comes on, you’ll notice the dance floor splits into two groups: people who know the steps and people awkwardly shuffling in circles. The song also runs over four minutes, which is a long stretch for a novelty track built around one hook.

The lyrics themselves are about a man who steals someone’s partner, an odd theme for a celebration of commitment. If you’re building your reception playlist, consider whether you want a song best known for its accordion-driven techno beat and line-dance routine representing your event.

15. “Cha Cha Slide” – DJ Casper

This track feels more like a workout video than a wedding moment. You get shouted instructions—slide to the left, slide to the right, criss cross—instead of music you actually want to dance to.

It works fine at a gym or a kid’s birthday party. At your wedding, it turns the dance floor into a choreography class.

The song also runs long, with verse after verse of new directions. Guests either commit fully or stand around waiting for it to end, and neither option adds much to your reception.

If you want your guests dancing together and enjoying themselves, this isn’t the song for it. Save it for casual parties where structured line dancing feels appropriate, and keep your wedding playlist focused on songs people choose to dance to, not ones that tell them how.

16. “Wobble” – V.I.C.

Released in 2008, “Wobble” turned into a line-dance staple that still shows up at weddings today. You’ve probably seen guests form rows and follow the steps without any prompting from the DJ.

The problem is the explicit content. Original lyrics aren’t suited for mixed-age crowds, so you’ll need a clean edit if kids or grandparents are on the guest list.

There’s also the crowd-split issue. Some guests love the choreography and rush the floor, while others sit out entirely, unsure of the steps or uninterested in line dances.

If you skip it, you won’t disappoint everyone. Line dances like this one divide opinion more than most other wedding song categories, and your reception can run just fine without it.

Consider your guest list’s age range and dance-floor habits before adding “Wobble” to your set list.

17. “Who Let the Dogs Out” – Baha Men

You released this song in 2000, and it became a genuine phenomenon. It hit number one in Australia and New Zealand, reached number two on the UK charts, and won a Grammy for Best Dance Recording in 2001. None of that makes it appropriate for your wedding.

The song works at baseball games and sports arenas, where a crowd shouts the hook between innings. It does not work when you’re trying to set a romantic mood for your first dance or dinner reception.

Your guests know this song from stadiums and novelty playlists, not love stories. Playing it during a wedding creates a jarring tonal shift that pulls people out of the moment. Save it for the reception’s dance floor chaos hour, if you must play it at all, but keep it far away from any meaningful moment in your ceremony.

18. “Mambo No. 5” – Lou Bega

You know this song the moment the horns hit. Released in 1999, it’s built on Dámaso Pérez Prado’s 1949 instrumental, and Bega added lyrics about a man juggling multiple women by name.

That’s the first problem. Angela, Pamela, Sandra, and Rita don’t belong in your wedding toast, let alone your first dance.

The song works at a bar or a birthday party. At a wedding, the lyrics undercut the whole point of the event you’re celebrating.

There’s also the pacing issue. It’s frantic, repetitive, and built for novelty rather than romance, so it clashes with almost every other song on your playlist.

If your goal is fun without irony, you have better options. This one reads as a joke, even when you don’t mean it that way.

19. “Single Ladies (Put a Ring on It)” – Beyoncé

You already know why this one is a problem. It’s about being single, not about getting married.

The song’s message centers on independence and warning an ex he missed his chance. That’s the opposite sentiment you want at a wedding reception.

If you play it, you’ll probably see people mimic the hand choreography, and someone will inevitably shout the “if you liked it” line at the wrong moment. It pulls focus onto Beyoncé’s dance moves rather than the couple.

The track works at bachelorette parties or as a fun throwback on a general dance floor. At a wedding, though, the lyrics undercut the occasion you’re celebrating.

You can still get people moving without the mismatched message. Save this one for another event and pick something that actually reflects commitment instead of singlehood.

20. “All About That Bass” – Meghan Trainor

This 2014 debut single put self-acceptance to a doo-wop beat, and it’s still a fun listen. That doesn’t mean it belongs on your wedding playlist.

The lyrics focus on body image and comparing yourself to other women, which isn’t the message you want floating around your reception. Some lines have also drawn criticism for putting down thinner body types while promoting confidence, an approach that feels mixed at best for a wedding crowd.

You want songs that speak to your relationship, not tracks built around a debate about body standards. The bouncy melody works fine for a car ride or a workout playlist.

At your wedding, guests are there to celebrate you and your partner, not sing along to a song about bass and treble.

21. “Blurred Lines” – Robin Thicke feat. T.I. and Pharrell

This 2013 track topped charts for weeks, but you should think twice before adding it to your wedding playlist. The lyrics carry connotations around consent that many guests find uncomfortable, especially at a celebration meant to honor commitment and respect.

The song also became one of the most controversial pop hits of its decade, tied to a high-profile copyright lawsuit and widespread criticism from music critics. That reputation follows it into any room where it plays.

Even if you enjoy the beat, consider how it lands with your guest list. A wedding crowd includes people of all ages and backgrounds, and this particular song has a track record of dividing opinion rather than uniting a dance floor.

If you want upbeat, feel-good music from this era, plenty of other options exist without the baggage.

22. “Baby Got Back” – Sir Mix-a-Lot

This 1992 hit is fun at parties. It is not fun when your grandmother is standing on the dance floor while the DJ plays lyrics about anacondas and getting “sprung.”

The song has been reframed over the years as a body-positivity anthem. That context doesn’t change the fact that it’s explicit, and weddings tend to have a wide range of ages and comfort levels in the room.

You’ll also run into a practical problem: most versions require heavy editing to be playable in front of family. Even edited, the innuendo is obvious enough that you’ll notice people looking uncomfortable.

If you want something upbeat and nostalgic from the same era, there are plenty of 90s tracks that won’t force you to explain the lyrics to your in-laws later.

23. “Pony” – Ginuwine

Released in 1996, “Pony” was written by Ginuwine with Static Major and Timbaland, who also produced the track. The lyrics are explicit about their intent, opening with a direct sexual invitation set to a stripped-down, synth-heavy beat.

You’ll recognize it instantly from its association with strip clubs, thanks in part to its use in the film “Magic Mike.” That connection alone should tell you it doesn’t belong at a wedding reception.

The song’s minor-key groove and suggestive lyrics create an odd mood shift when played during dinner or a first dance. Guests often laugh, cringe, or both.

If you want a genuine R&B moment on your playlist, there are better Ginuwine-era tracks that don’t require explaining to your grandmother why everyone’s laughing.

24. “Hot in Herre” – Nelly

“Hot in Herre” hit number one in 2002 and stayed on the radio for years afterward. That familiarity is exactly why it doesn’t belong on your wedding playlist.

The lyrics are explicit. Nelly wrote the song about a room getting too warm because people are taking their clothes off. Playing this while grandparents share a table with young cousins puts everyone in an uncomfortable spot.

You also lose control of the mood once it comes on. The song demands a certain kind of dancing, and that energy doesn’t match a formal reception or a quiet family gathering.

If you want a nostalgic 2000s hip-hop moment, pick something with cleaner lyrics. Your guests will still recognize the era without you having to explain the words to a curious child later.

25. “Closer” – Nine Inch Nails

You know this song from its chorus, which repeats a line about wanting to have sex in explicit terms. That alone should tell you it doesn’t belong at your reception.

“Closer” appeared on Nine Inch Nails’ 1994 album The Downward Spiral, and it’s an industrial rock track built around dark, obsessive themes rather than romance. Trent Reznor wrote it about degradation and need, not commitment or love.

You might think the pounding beat makes it danceable, but the lyrics will make your grandmother’s jaw drop. Some couples have used it ironically for entrances, betting on shock value, but that approach doesn’t always land well with older relatives or conservative guests.

If you want industrial or alternative sounds at your wedding, choose something with cleaner lyrical content. Save this one for a different occasion entirely.

26. “Bed of Roses” – Bon Jovi

You’ve probably heard this one at a reception, drifting from the speakers during a slow dance. It sounds romantic on the surface, with soaring vocals and a piano-driven build. That’s exactly the problem.

“Bed of Roses” was written by Jon Bon Jovi in a hotel room, and the lyrics reflect a man on tour, drinking, and missing someone while wrestling with guilt. It’s a song about loneliness and infidelity, not commitment.

If you listen closely, you’ll notice lines about wanting to be “somebody’s baby” and wishing for forgiveness. That’s not what you want echoing through your first dance.

You can appreciate the song’s emotional depth without putting it on your wedding playlist. Save it for a road trip instead. Your guests will thank you, and so will your marriage.

27. “You Give Love a Bad Name” – Bon Jovi

You might love this song at a rock concert, but a wedding is a different setting entirely.

Songwriter Desmond Child originally wrote an early version of this melody for Bonnie Tyler before reworking it with Jon Bon Jovi and Richie Sambora. The result became one of the band’s biggest hits, driven by Sambora’s guitar riff and an unmistakable chorus.

The problem is right there in the title. You’re celebrating a marriage, and the lyrics are about betrayal and heartbreak.

If you play this at a reception, you’re putting a song about a “bad name” and shattered trust into a moment meant to celebrate commitment. The energy works for a bar or a road trip playlist, not for a first dance or a toast.

Save it for another occasion. Your wedding guests will thank you.

28. “Love Stinks” – The J. Geils Band

You know this one. It shows up on wedding playlists more often than you’d expect, usually as a joke request from someone at the reception.

The problem is right there in the title. Peter Wolf and Seth Justman wrote it as a bitter rant about unrequited love, not a celebration of finding it.

The lyrics list off two people who have everything and one person who has nothing, ending with the flat verdict that love stinks. That’s a strange message to play at an event built around a couple committing to each other.

You might think it works as a lighthearted joke, but guests won’t always read it that way. Playing a song about love being miserable at a wedding sends mixed signals, even if you mean it ironically.

Save it for a different playlist.

29. “You’re So Vain” – Carly Simon

You might love this song, but its lyrics make it a strange choice for a wedding.

The track is a takedown of a self-absorbed ex-lover. Carly Simon wrote it about someone who thought the world revolved around him. That’s not exactly the sentiment you want hanging over your first dance.

The chorus alone gives away the problem. “You’re so vain, you probably think this song is about you” is not a line that celebrates commitment or love.

Even if the melody sounds smooth and nostalgic, the words tell a different story. It’s a song about disappointment, not devotion.

If you play it at your reception, don’t be surprised if guests raise an eyebrow. Save it for a playlist that has nothing to do with vows.

30. “Tainted Love” – Soft Cell

Soft Cell released “Tainted Love” in 1981 on their album Non-Stop Erotic Cabaret. The lyrics describe a relationship that has turned toxic and destructive.

If you play this at your wedding, you’re setting an odd tone. The song is about wanting to escape love, not celebrate it.

Lines like “I’ve got to get away” and “once I ran to you, now I’ll run from you” don’t fit a first dance or reception moment. Guests who know the lyrics will notice the disconnect immediately.

The synth-pop energy might tempt you if you’re going for a retro dance vibe. But the words matter here, and they work against the occasion you’re marking.

Save this one for a different playlist. Your wedding day deserves songs that actually reflect commitment, not the desire to flee from it.

Why a Song Can Feel Wrong at a Wedding

A song can sound perfect on the radio but feel off the moment it plays at your ceremony or reception. The mismatch usually comes down to two things: what the words actually say, and when you choose to play them.

Lyrics Versus Familiar Melodies

You often recognize a song by its melody long before you register the lyrics. This is why upbeat tracks about breakups, obsession, or infidelity end up on wedding playlists by mistake.

“Every Breath You Take” is a common example. The tune sounds romantic, but the lyrics describe surveillance and control, not love.

Here’s what to check before adding a song to your list:

  • Read the full lyrics, not just the chorus you remember.
  • Look up the song’s backstory, since some tracks reference cheating or heartbreak despite a cheerful sound.
  • Ask someone else to listen critically, since you may be too familiar with the tune to notice the words.

A song that feels celebratory on the surface can carry a message you don’t want attached to your marriage.

How Timing and Audience Change the Impact

The same song can work in one moment and fail in another. A slow ballad might suit your first dance but stall the energy if you play it during peak dancing hours.

Your guest list also matters. A song with explicit language or a niche reference may land well with your friend group but confuse or alienate older relatives.

How to Keep the Music Right for Your Celebration

You can prevent most wedding music mistakes by checking song content ahead of time and giving your DJ or band specific direction. These two steps catch problems before they reach the dance floor.

Review Lyrics and Clean Versions Before Booking

Read through the full lyrics of every song on your list before you finalize your playlist. A song might sound romantic in the chorus but shift to explicit or negative content in later verses.

Many popular songs have “clean” or “radio edit” versions that remove profanity and inappropriate references. Check whether your chosen tracks have these versions available, and specify which version you want in your written agreement.

Pay attention to context, not just individual words. A breakup song without profanity can still feel wrong at a wedding if the lyrics describe cheating, divorce, or resentment.

Ask yourself these questions for each song:

  • Does the song reference infidelity, death, or breakups?
  • Are there explicit lyrics in any verse, even if the chorus is clean?
  • Does the meaning match the moment you’re using it for (first dance, entrance, etc.)?

Give Your DJ or Band Clear Do-Not-Play Guidance

Create a written do-not-play list and share it with your DJ or band at least two weeks before the wedding. Include specific song titles, not just genres or artists, since some artists have both suitable and unsuitable tracks.

Specify whether you want explicit lyrics avoided entirely or only during certain parts of the event, such as the ceremony or dinner hour. Some couples allow explicit songs during late-night dancing but not during cocktail hour.

Give your DJ authority to skip requests from guests that conflict with your list. Confirm this arrangement directly with them, since guests sometimes push for songs you’ve already excluded.

Provide a backup contact, such as a wedding planner or bridal party member, who can answer questions if you’re unavailable during the event.

title: The 10 Best Goo Goo Dolls Songs of All-Time
content:
In 1986, guitarist/vocalist John Rzeznik, bassist/vocalist Robby Takac, and drummer George Tutuska formed the Goo Goo Dolls. They started as a cover band, dabbled with punk, and eventually settled on alt-rock. After 12 years and five albums, they finally hit the big time in 1998 with the hit single, Iris. Since then, the band has gone on to sell over 15 million records worldwide, picking up four Grammy Award nominations and 19 top ten singles in the process. Here’s our pick of the 10 best Goo Goo Dolls songs of all time.

10. Can’t Let It Go

As Louder Sound says, the Goo Goo Dolls’ 2006 album Let Love In is uneven and tired sounding in parts, but it still has a few classic anthems in the mix. Of those, Can’t Let It Go is one of the best. It doesn’t waste any time getting to the chorus, and considering Rzeznik’s talent for a killer chorus, that’s no bad thing at all. It didn’t get the single treatment, but of all the songs on the album, this is the one that deserved it the most.

9. All Eyes On Me

The band’s sixth studio album, Dizzy Up The Girl, is widely regarded as the one that helped send their career into orbit. In fairness, a lot of that comes down to the success of their No. 1 hit, Iris, but one song alone doesn’t make an album sell over 4 million. Much of the success of Dizzy Up The Girl lies in the deep cuts, of which the haunting All Eyes On Me is one of the greatest. Featuring hushed verses, a massive chorus, and some very bracing drumming from new drummer Mike Malinin, it’s an underrated gem.

8. Big Machine

Johnny Rzeznik calls Big Machine “his disco song.” His definition of disco might be a little different from ours, but disco or not, it does find the band breaking free of their comfort zone and getting a little free and easy with their usual rhythms. As usual, the hook is massive and the chorus is catchy – both Goo Goo Dolls trademarks, and both done exceptionally well here. Released as a single from the band’s 2002 album, Gutterflower, it climbed to No. 64 on the Billboard Hot 100 and No. 10 on the Billboard Adult Top 40 chart.

7. Broadway

The Goo Goo Dolls’ big breakthrough came with Dizzy Up The Girl, and so did some of their biggest hits. Although Broadway didn’t climb quite as high on the charts as the album’s first two singles (Iris and Slide), it still managed to reach a very respectable No. 24 on the Billboard Hot 100 and No. 24 on the Billboard year-end Hot 100 singles of 2000. According to Genius, Rzeznik took his inspiration for the song from his hometown of Buffalo, where most of the blue-collar workers spent their free time drinking away the hours. As he got older, he noticed the next generation was falling into the exact same habits. Lyrically, it takes its lead from Bruce Springsteen, but that adrenalin-pumping chorus is pure Goo Goo Dolls.

6. Amigone

According to The Cheese Life, Amigone was supposedly named after a funeral parlor in the Dolls’ hometown of Buffalo, NY. If it is, the slightly morbid theme hasn’t infected the song, which is a fast-paced, hard-driven slice of rock with some ace drumming from Mike Malinin and stellar vocals from bassist Robby Takac.

5. Black Balloon

Iris was the song that got everyone talking about the Goo Goo Dolls and sent copies of Dizzy Up The Girl flying off the shelves, but it’s by no means the only good song on the album. Black Balloon, for example, is an absolute banger, with a gritty vocal from Reznik and a stunningly accomplished performance from the rest of the band. If any song helped transform the perception of the Goo Goo Dolls from a bunch of alt-rock amateurs into serious contenders, this was it. Released in June 1999 as the fourth single from the album, it took the band to No. 16 on the US Billboard Hot 100.

4. Name

Although Iris turned the band into a household name, their first major hit was actually released three years earlier. Taken from the album A Boy Named Goo, Name took the band to the top of both the US Modern Rock Tracks chart and the Album Rock Tracks chart and peaked at No. 5 on the Billboard Hot 100. It was inspired by Rzeznik’s turbulent relationship with former MTV VJ Lisa Kennedy Montgomery. “I was trying to capture a moment…it was pretty interesting to have a song inspired by a moment. And I thought it was a very sweet song,” Rzeznik has explained.

3. Ain’t that Unusual

Ain’t that Unusual is a song about losers. Unlike most songs about losers, it doesn’t offer a light at the end of the tunnel. “Someday you never made it,’ Rzeznik sings, ‘maybe you never will.” Fortunately, the riffs and chorus are both big enough to stop it from falling into abject misery. Recorded for the 1995 album A Boy Named Goo, it’s an excellent example of just how innovative the band can sound when they put their minds to it.

2. Long Way Down

Long Way Down distills everything there is to love about the Goo Goo Dolls in less than 3 and a half minutes. It’s a little rough and ready, a tiny bit naive, and has just enough grit to counter the sentimentality of the lyrics. Rzeznik’s raspy performance is dynamite, while the chorus is, as you’d expect, powerful enough to stop an army. Released as the fifth single from 1995’s A Boy Named Goo, it didn’t reach quite the same heights of glory as the album’s other big single, Name, but it still managed to claim to No. 7 on the Billboard Mainstream Rock Tracks chart and No. 25 on the Modern Rock Tracks chart.

1. Iris

Sure, it’s predictable, but sometimes, the most obvious choice is obvious for a reason. Iris was the song that turned the Goo Goo Dolls from alt-rock pretenders into chart-topping contenders. Released on April 1, 1998, it’s one of the biggest crossover hits of all time, becoming the most played song of 1998 on pop, modern rock, and adult contemporary radio. It climbed to No. 9 on the US Billboard Hot 100, No. 3 in the UK, and topped the charts in Australia, Canada, and Italy. The Goo Goo Dolls never managed to top its success… then again, what band could?

title: OutKast Retrospective Opens At Atlanta’s Trap Music Museum
content:
Step into the Dungeon and walk out through the stars.

Atlanta’s Trap Music Museum invites you to experience OutKast: a definitive retrospective honoring the duo whose sound redefined the South and reshaped hip-hop as we know it. Since the early 1990s, André 3000 and Big Boi have carried Atlanta’s voice onto the world stage, proving that greatness doesn’t have to come from New York or Los Angeles to matter. This exhibit traces that full arc, from their earliest days recording in Organized Noize’s legendary Dungeon studio to the global acclaim, three Grammy wins, and lasting cultural legacy that followed. Original paintings throughout the gallery bring their story to vivid life, including the cosmic “Mighty O” painting by C. Ray, a “Ms. Jackson”-inspired piece by Trinity Nixon, and a version of the Stankonia album cover made of coffee beans.

A bold cubist portrait by Jerell Gantt sets the duo against an American flag backdrop, while an immersive Afrofuturist installation, lit in violet and framed in reclaimed wood, pulls visitors into the mystical, 1970s-inspired world that shaped their visual identity. Rare memorabilia and iconic wardrobe pieces round out the experience, anchored by André 3000’s black flight jumpsuit from OutKast’s 2014 reunion tour, hand-painted with the question that still echoes today: “across cultures, darker people suffer most. why?” Come celebrate the artistry, the Atlanta roots, and the enduring voice of two of hip-hop’s most original storytellers.

title: SZA To Headline Coachella 2027, Nearly A Decade After Last Solo Set
content:
SZA is no stranger to performing at Coachella, but her next appearance will still feel like a full-circle moment.

The seven-time Grammy Award-winning singer will join Dua Lipa and Tame Impala as headliners for the 2027 festival. Coachella returns to Indio, California, for two weekends, April 9-11 and April 16-18, 2027.

SZA will close out the festival’s third day on both weekends, marking her first time headlining the event.

The R&B superstar last appeared at Coachella in April 2026, when she joined Justin Bieber during his headlining set. The two surprised fans with a performance of their collaboration, “Snooze.”

However, SZA’s history with the festival stretches back much further. She previously performed a full set in 2018, during the early stages of her rise to superstardom. Nearly a decade later, she’ll return as one of the biggest names on the entire lineup.

SZA Leads Coachella’s R&B Lineup As Hip-Hop Takes A Back Seat

While SZA leads a strong group of R&B performers, Hip-Hop has a noticeably smaller presence among Coachella’s top-billed acts in 2027.

Don Toliver, Freddie Gibbs, Fetty Wap and several emerging rappers are among the scheduled performers. Still, no traditional rap artist holds one of the festival’s three main headlining positions.

R&B fans, meanwhile, have plenty to look forward to. Kehlani, Leon Thomas, Steve Lacy, Mariah the Scientist, Victoria Monét and Jorja Smith are among the artists scheduled to perform.

The lineup also reflects a shift from previous festivals. In 2024, Tyler, the Creator and Doja Cat occupied headlining spots, while Travis Scott received special billing in 2025.

Although Hip-Hop remains part of the festival, its biggest stars aren’t dominating the marquee this time around.

Still, SZA’s headlining appearance represents a major moment for contemporary R&B. Her journey from an emerging festival performer to a Grammy-winning headliner highlights just how far her career has come.

title: Yella Beezy Convicted In Mo3 Murder Case
content:
The Yella Beezy and MO3 murder trial has come to a close as the jury reached its verdict on November 11, 2026. 

This week, the defense brought in private investigator and digital forensics expert Brian Ingram to break down cellphone records and location data. Ingram testified that Beezy’s phone frequently connected to cell towers near his Frisco home, gym, and a Drury Inn. He also presented GPS records showing Kewon White’s phone at Devin Brown’s home at 2:49 p.m. on the day MO3 was killed.

The defense also called Beezy’s aunt, cousin, and longtime hairstylist to the stand. His aunt testified that Beezy regularly helped support family members financially, sometimes giving relatives between $10,000 and $30,000 for bills and other expenses. She also explained that a $10,000 wire transfer was meant to help cover temporary hotel lodging while the family prepared to move.

His cousin confirmed picking up money wired to his mother, while his hairstylist testified about appointments with Beezy in Oak Cliff shortly before the murder.

Dallas rapper Yella Beezy was convicted and sentenced to life in prison in the murder-for-hire case involving rival rapper MO3. The guilty verdict was delivered on the sixth anniversary of the murder.

Yella Beezy, whose real name is Markies Conway, was accused of paying another man to gun down Dallas rapper Mo3 in an ambush on Interstate 35 in 2020. Prosecutors said Conway hired kewon white to carry out the killing over a long-running feud. Kewon has also been sentenced to life in prison without parole

Conway pled not guilty and denied his involvement; White was previously convicted of capital murder for Melvin Noble’s death. 

A third defendant, devin brown, is also charged with capital murder and is still awaiting trial.

title: Master P’s Son Hercy Miller Will Play His Father In Snoop Dogg Biopic
content:
The casting news for the upcoming Snoop Dogg biopic keeps getting better, and the latest addition brings a little family connection to the big screen. Hercy Miller, the son of rap mogul Master P, has officially been cast to play his father in the highly anticipated film.

According to Deadline, the role will mark Miller’s feature film debut. Not exactly a bad way to get your Hollywood career started, considering he’ll be portraying one of hip-hop’s most recognizable figures in a movie about one of its biggest stars.

Miller joins a growing cast that includes P-Valley actor Zachariah Rogers, who will portray rapper and producer The D.O.C., and Tyquan Givens, who has been tapped to play an original character named B. Mack.

The film, titled Snoop, is scheduled to hit theaters on Aug. 6, 2027, with Universal Pictures behind the project. The studio has some experience bringing hip-hop stories to the big screen, having produced the 2015 N.W.A. biopic Straight Outta Compton and Eminem’s 8 Mile. So there’s reason to hope the studio can give Snoop’s story the treatment it deserves.

Other recently announced casting includes Cynthia Erivo as Afeni Shakur, the mother of the late Tupac Shakur. Jonathan Daviss, Myles Bullock, Lauren London, Camron Jones, Algee Smith, Tre Hale, Laya DeLeon Hayes, Olly Sholotan, Corey Champagne, Jonica Booth and SwayvoTwain are also among the cast members.

Craig Brewer, whose previous directing credits include Hustle & Flow and Song Sung Blue, will direct the project. Snoop himself will serve as a producer alongside Brian Grazer and Sara Ramaker for Death Row Pictures.

There’s plenty of hip-hop history to cover, from Snoop’s rise out of Long Beach to his partnership with Dr. Dre and his transformation into a global entertainment icon. The addition of Master P’s son only adds another interesting layer to a story that will inevitably feature some of rap’s most influential figures.

And Snoop hasn’t exactly been keeping a low profile lately. The rapper recently joined JAY-Z and Dr. Dre onstage at SoFi Stadium during the Los Angeles stop of the JAŸ30 celebrations.

With the August 2027 release date approaching, more casting announcements and details are likely on the way.

title: Cam Newton Accuses Ex of Drug Abuse, Seeks Full Custody
content:
Media personality and former NFL star Cam Newton has returned to court, demanding full custody of his children and claiming his ex, Kia Proctor has “substance abuse issues” which prompted his decision.

According to reports, the former Carolina Panthers quarterback filed a petition last Friday (November 6) in Fulton County Superior Court requesting full custody of the four children he shares with Proctor – Chosen (born 2015), Sovereign-Dior (2017), Camidas (2018) and Cashmere (2019). Newton has even alleged that Proctor isn’t interested in building relationships between the children and their half-siblings. Newton has five other children from other relationships, making nine in total including two with actress Jasmine Brown.

The two had been a couple during the bulk of his NFL career, from 2013 to 2020. Proctor has not responded publicly to the filing. title: Judge Dismisses Birdman From Lil Wayne Tour Bus Shooting Lawsuit
content:
Birdman can cross one more legal headache off his list. The Cash Money Records co-founder has been dismissed from a decade-old lawsuit filed by a former Lil Wayne tour bus driver over the infamous 2015 shooting that left two tour buses riddled with bullets outside Atlanta.

Alvin Lewis, who was driving one of Lil Wayne’s tour buses at the time, filed suit against Birdman and Cash Money Records, alleging assault and battery, breach of contract and intentional infliction of emotional distress. But according to TMZ, a judge ruled Tuesday that Birdman and his record label should be dismissed from the case.

The judge reportedly determined that Birdman was not in the same state when the shooting occurred and that there was insufficient evidence connecting him to the incident. The ruling also noted that Lewis was never struck by a bullet or shrapnel during the attack.

That doesn’t mean Lewis walked away unscathed, at least according to his claims. The former driver has maintained that the incident caused him emotional distress and resulted in lost income.

Birdman, however, won’t have to answer for those allegations in this particular lawsuit. And after roughly 10 years of litigation, that’s a pretty significant legal victory for the rap executive.

The lawsuit also involved rapper Young Thug and Jimmy “PeeWee Roscoe” Winfrey, who was sentenced to 10 years in prison followed by 10 years of probation for his role in the shooting.

The incident happened April 26, 2015, after Lil Wayne performed at Atlanta’s Compound nightclub. Two tour buses traveling along Interstate 285 were fired upon multiple times. Although nobody was physically injured, the shooting became a major hip-hop story because of the high-profile names involved and the questions surrounding who was responsible.

Winfrey was ultimately convicted in connection with the shooting, while Young Thug’s alleged involvement also became part of the broader legal controversy.

Lewis’ lawsuit is not entirely over, despite Tuesday’s ruling. The case can continue against the remaining defendants, but Birdman and Cash Money Records are officially out of this particular legal fight.

For the man who helped build one of hip-hop’s most recognizable record labels, it’s one less courtroom appearance to worry about.

title: Ranking All the Daft Punk Studio Albums
content:
Daft Punk were one of the most notable duos in electronic music and beyond. For those who are unfamiliar, Guy-Manuel de Homem-Christo and Thomas Bangalter worked together until 2021, which was when they went their separate ways for unknown reasons. In that time, Daft Punk released four studio albums plus a soundtrack album. On the whole, they have been well-received, so much so that chances are good that interested individuals have heard one or more of their songs at some point in time.

5. Human After All

Sometimes, the people who make art can have very different opinions from the people who experience that same art. To name an example, consider Human After All, which was Daft Punk’s third studio album. At the time, they considered it to be their favorite studio album, stating that it had a close connection to their own experiences. Furthermore, Human After All was apparently capable of showing moments of beauty in between a general sense of fear and sadness inspired by the less pleasant aspects of technology.

Meanwhile, the critics were less enamored. Essentially, this was based on the fact that Human After All was a very different album from its two predecessors. Those had been inspired by a combination of disco and garage house. In contrast, this was a much more minimalistic, much more improvisational sound made using just six pieces of equipment for the most part. Theoretically, there is no reason why such works can’t please. In practice, well, the critics simply weren’t pleased.

4. Tron: Legacy

Human imagination tends to outstrip human advancement. For proof, look no further than 1982’s Tron, which came into existence because its creator became fascinated by video games upon seeing Pong for the first time. On the whole, the movie met with a mixed reception. Critics liked the acting as well as the visuals that went with the acting.

However, they weren’t too thrilled by the story, which they considered incoherent. Still, Tron proved to be influential, so much so that it received a follow-up called Tron: Legacy in 2010. Amusingly, said movie proved to be very popular to its predecessor. Once more, it received a mixed reception. On the one hand, the critics were less than impressed by either the cast or the story that the cast members were working with; on the other hand, the critics loved the visuals, the music, and the production.

Thanks to that, Tron: Legacy has become something of a cult classic in its own right. By 2010, Daft Punk had more than managed to make their name. As such, they were the natural choice for Tron: Legacy’s soundtrack album, as shown by how they were sought out by the movie’s director for the job. The result isn’t quite what interested individuals might expect based on Daft Punk’s other work. However, there is a reason that its music is considered to be one of Tron: Legacy’s selling points, meaning that the soundtrack album is well-worth listening to.

3. Homework

There aren’t a lot of studio albums that can be called banner-bearers for entire music genres. However, Homework is one of them. After all, it didn’t just make Daft Punk known to the world, it made French house music as a whole known to the world. Unsurprisingly, that meant that Homework was extremely influential on both its own music genre and international dance music as a whole. In any case, it is interesting to note that Daft Punk didn’t break out onto the world stage with the release of their first studio album.

Instead, they had already been making a name for themselves, so much so that there was a bidding war between record labels for the duo’s work. Eventually, Daft Punk produced enough singles that they figured that they had enough material for a full-fledged studio album. As it turned out, their belief was quite correct because Homework went on to sell millions of copies. In hindsight, Homework loses some points for incoherency. However, it nonetheless remains a remarkable collection of songs even if that remarkable collection of songs happens to be a bit hodgepodge in certain places.

2. Random Access Memories

A lot of people will remember Random Access Memories. This is because Daft Punk’s fourth studio album was also one of their most successful studio albums. In particular, it is worth mentioning that this was their one studio album to hit the number one position on the U.S. Billboard 200 as well as the number one position on similar charts in 20 other countries. Quite a bit of this momentum came from the overwhelming success of its lead single “Get Lucky,” which sold so many copies that it has since become recognized as one of the best-selling singles of all time. The commercial success of Random Access Memories was matched by its critical success.

There are those who champion it as one of the best studio albums of the 2010s. Moreover, it did very well in its year’s award shows, as shown by how it claimed not one, not two, but five Grammy Awards in 2014. Music-wise, Random Access Memories was something of a risk. After all, it wasn’t a return to Daft Punk’s earlier work. Instead, it was an attempt at overcoming the not so enthusiastic response to Human After All by weaving in live instrumentation and other novel elements that the duo had never done before. As such, the success of Random Access Memories was that much more impressive by showing Daft Punk’s ability to outdo themselves.

1. Discovery

Random Access Memories is a strong contender. However, it is beaten out by Discovery, which can be considered Daft Punk’s most iconic studio album. If Homework was raw and unpolished, then its successor can be considered the finished product. As such, it is no wonder that it managed to become both a critical and a commercial success, which proved to be influential enough to reshape the house music scene once again.

It is interesting to note that Discovery saw Daft Punk teaming up with the Japanese mangaka Matsumoto Reiji to create an anime movie that had no dialogue but instead used the studio album as its soundtrack. Older individuals who saw the music video for “One More Time” might have found it familiar. This is because Matsumoto is a well-known figure in his own right who has a very distinctive visual style.

title: Coachella 2027 Lineup Is Here: Dua Lipa, Tame Impala and SZA
content:
Coachella Valley Music and Arts Festival has officially unveiled the full lineup for 2027, and Goldenvoice is swinging for the fences with a mix of first-time headliners, returning favorites and a few curveballs nobody saw coming. The announcement landed Wednesday, Nov. 11, and within minutes the internet was dissecting every name on the poster, from the top line down to the fine print.

The headline trio is Dua Lipa on Friday, Tame Impala on Saturday and SZA on Sunday. For Lipa, this is her first time topping the Coachella bill, though she is no stranger to the polo fields. She appeared as a guest during Martin Garrix’s set in 2017, and her 2024 album Radical Optimism featured production from Kevin Parker, the man behind Tame Impala. Parker’s warm, psychedelic production gave that record some of its best moments. Tame Impala returns to the headlining slot after his 2019 set, a performance that cemented Parker as one of the festival’s most reliable live acts. SZA rounds out the weekend with her first proper headlining set. She played Coachella in 2016 and 2018 and popped up during Justin Bieber’s 2026 set.

The top line is only part of the story. Coachella 2027 has a few special slots that give the weekend extra weight. Daddy Yankee has been tapped for a fourth top-billed position with a special production, which points to something bigger than a standard set. Justice is on the poster with a Bunker debut of “Blinded by the Lights,” which should give electronic fans something to circle in red ink. And Madonna returns to the Dance Tent, a space she last played in 2006 during the Confessions on a Dance Floor era. For longtime attendees, that is a deep cut, and it shows the festival is paying attention to its own history, not just the current charts.

Friday’s undercard is deep, with names that could easily headline smaller festivals. Zara Larsson, Steve Lacy, Jisoo, Kehlani and Leon Thomas all sit in the upper tiers, giving the first night a pop and R&B lean that should keep the crowd moving from the moment the gates open. Saturday shifts gears with Phoebe Bridgers, Weezer, Tiësto, Martin Garrix, Robyn, Role Model and Maneskin, a lineup that jumps from indie rock to big-room dance music. Sunday closes things out with Don Toliver, Dom Dolla, Kygo, Becky G, Remi Wolf, Tove Lo, Victoria Monét and BABYMONSTER, a mix that should appeal to just about anyone who has ever set foot in the desert. Friday leans pop and R&B, Saturday is heavier on rock and dance, and Sunday splits the difference.

The full poster goes deeper. Four Tet, Caroline Polachek, Underworld, Peggy Gou, Giorgio Moroder, Magdalena Bay and Gang of Youths are scattered across the lower lines, which means the real heads will have plenty of reasons to show up early and stay late. Coachella has always been as much about discovery as it is about the headliners, and this year’s bill seems designed to reward the people who do their homework before the gates open.

The festival returns to the Empire Polo Club in Indio, California, for two weekends: April 9-11 and April 16-18, 2027. Passes go on sale Friday, Nov. 13 at noon PT, and if history is any indication, you will want to be at your computer a few minutes early. YouTube is back for its 15th year as the exclusive livestream partner, so even if you cannot make it to the desert, you can watch both weekends from wherever you happen to be. Hotel packages bundling passes with lodging and transportation are also available for anyone who wants to avoid the scramble for accommodations.

The 2027 announcement arrives on the heels of a strong 2026 edition that featured headlining sets from Sabrina Carpenter, Justin Bieber and Karol G. Coachella has built its reputation on reinvention, and this lineup moves in a new direction while still honoring the artists who built it. Pop fans, indie loyalists and anyone who just wants to dance in the desert until the sun comes up all have a reason to show up. The only question left is whether you will be there in person or watching from the couch with the livestream cranked up.

title: XS Is Back, and It Was Worth the Wait: Inside the Wynn Club’s Grand Reopening Weekend
content:
XS’s grand reopening weekend is in the books, and the verdict is in: the wait was worth it.

Four nights, four headliners: RÜFÜS DU SOL opening with a DJ set Thursday, The Chainsmokers Friday, Calvin Harris Saturday, and Diplo B2B Hugel closing it out Sunday. For a club that first opened on New Year’s Eve 2008 and went on to host residencies from Avicii, Tiësto, and David Guetta, it was the most on-brand comeback imaginable.

It was also a homecoming.
