title: Haywire sign to Roadrunner, announce new LP & video, threw $$ into the crowd at Sound & Fury, keep touring & stuff (BV-exclusive vinyl)
content:
Boston punks Haywire are one of the fastest rising hardcore bands of recent times, and now they’ve announced their second full-length album, I Don’t Wanna Say Goodbye, due October 2 via their new label home, Roadrunner Records. Citizen‘s Mat Kerekes produced the album. Taylor Young mixed it at The Pit. The album was recorded over three months in Leeds, UK and Toledo, OH, and features appearances from members of Nothing and The Aggrolites, along with other friends of the band.

We’ve teamed up with the band for a BrooklynVegan-exclusive vinyl variant of I Don’t Wanna Say Goodbye, limited to just 300 copies. Pre-order now in the BV Shop.

The first single from I Don’t Wanna Say Goodbye is “Interstate Love Affair,” which comes with a Luis Hernandez-directed video. Watch it below.

It follows Haywire’s 2024 great releases, the Conditioned for Demolition LP and For Better or for Worse EP, and 2025 splits with No Guard and Dropkick Murphys ( “Citizen I.C.E.” included).

Constantly on the road (and in our feeds), last year Haywire completed a goal of playing all 50 states, and played an amazing tour with Drain, No Pressure and Secret World. They’re taking a short unexpected break though. They announced this morning that their Australia tour this week is postponed till later in the year, but they’ll be touring again in the US in September, including a Milwaukee show supporting Turnstile, a run opening for Circle Jerks, and appearances at Louder Than Life, Riot Fest, Four Chord Music Festival and CBGB Fest. October brings Aftershock, Furnace Fest, a free University of Connecticut show and Sick New World, followed by Pressure Point Fest and Warped Tour in November.

Haywire revealed that they’d signed to Roadrunner just ahead of this past weekend’s Sound & Fury fest, then celebrated their new record deal by throwing $5,000 in cash into the crowd during their set on Sunday. Watch footage below.

Sunday at Sound & Fury also included a surprise split set from Twitching Tongues and God’s Hate, both bands of brothers Colin and Taylor Young (the same Taylor who worked on the new Haywire album) (and the new Terror record and a million other records). A day after the surprise appearance, God’s Hate revealed that they were ending their hiatus with a new three-song Won’t Be Disgraced EP.

title: Fontaines D.C. announce new album ‘Dopamine Chamber,’ share ‘Marianne,’ sang with Kurt Vile
content:
Fontaines D.C. have announced their fifth album, Dopamine Chamber, due October 16 via XL Recordings. They reunited with producer James Ford, who also produced its 2024 predecessor, the Grammy-nominated Romance, which we called their best album yet in Bill’s review on release day, and which we went on to name the 6th best album of that year.

They made the album between London, the English countryside and Palermo, where Grian Chatten recorded vocals in a makeshift booth built from mattresses and cushions. He also spent time in Venice, Vienna and Sicily looking for lyrical inspiration. Dopamine Chamber is available on LP, deluxe LP, CD, cassette and digital, and you can preorder it from the BrooklynVegan shop.

The announcement follows Fontaines D.C.’s recent return to the stage for their first shows in nearly a year. They played a BBC session at Maida Vale on July 31 before returning to regular live shows in Spain earlier this month, where they began debuting new material, including “Marianne.”

They’ve now shared “Marianne” as the album’s lead single. The song was partly inspired by the 2024 series Ripley, and deals with escapism and hedonism.

For Dopamine Chamber, Fontaines D.C. brought synthesizers, samples, triggers, marching drums and strings influenced by 1960s Italian pop into the mix, and several songs don’t feature guitars at all. “I was trying to find stuff that pointed into the future,” guitarist Conor Curley says.

“The album itself is a dopamine chamber,” Grian says. “You step inside and we test these different mind- or mood-altering pieces of music on you.”

Grian also says:

“I think Romance was maybe 60 per cent human and 40 per cent corrupted by automation, and a loss of feeling. This one feels more like 60 per cent corrupted — the mask is wearing the face a little more. I felt it would be more powerful to leave the hope out and reflect the ugliness honestly. This one needed to feel more like a catastrophic warning.”

Bassist Conor Deegan adds:

“Our albums have always questioned a sense of place. First Dublin, then being away from Dublin, and then trying to find the romance elsewhere. On this record, the question became: where do you escape to?”

Fontaines D.C. headlined La Route du Rock in France on Saturday (8/15), where they brought out special guest Kurt Vile to join them for “Roman Holiday.” This was especially cool because Grian cited Vile as an inspiration for the Skinty Fia song in a 2022 Rolling Stone UK interview, saying:

“It’s easy listening first, through songs like ‘Roman Holiday.’ I’d say that song was quite inspired by Kurt Vile; I saw him play in Croatia two years ago when we were playing there and I envied him. The sun was going down and he was able to stand there and chill out. We spend ten minutes before going on stage slapping each other in the face! I envy someone who can send a text to his kid, go off on stage and then just play really well.”

Watch Fontaines D.C. and Vile play “Roman Holiday” together below.

Fontaines D.C. have been busy elsewhere, too. They released “It’s Amazing To Be Young” as a standalone single in 2025, before including it as one of the few bonus tracks on the deluxe edition of Romance. This year, they covered Sinéad O’Connor’s “Black Boys on Mopeds” for War Child’s HELP(2) benefit compilation. Grian also teamed with Damon Albarn and Kae Tempest for the album’s “Flags.”

Kurt Vile, meanwhile, released his 10th album, Philadelphia’s been good to me, in May (get it on vinyl in the BV shop).

Fontaines D.C. are currently back on the road, with Reading, Leeds and Electric Picnic coming up later this month. They return to the US in September for Shaky Knees in Atlanta, Sea.Hear.Now in Asbury Park and Ohana Festival in Dana Point. All currently announced dates are below.

title: The Still Out reissue coming; song w/ Adam Franklin of Swervedriver (who they reformed to open for) out now
content:
New York City indie rock band The Still Out — who we recently mentioned were reforming to open some shows for their friends in Swervedriver —  formed in the late 2000s by producers Josh Stoddard and Arjun “Arj” Agerwala. Stoddard tragically passed away in 2021, and Agerwala is reforming the band and reissuing their 2008 album Crystallized in tribute to his best friend and bandmate. 

Crystallized has been off streaming services for a while, but returns on Friday, August 21 with the release of a deluxe, remastered edition.  Agerwala tells us:

We didn’t make the record for anyone but ourselves. It has taken me nearly five years to recover from Josh’s death. It feels fitting, now that I’m able, to share our vision and bring something beautiful out of that darkness. This album is now both a tribute to him and a literal record of our friendship and creative journey together. I want anyone who may be into this to be able to hear it. It also feels like a tribute to our mentor Adam Schlesinger [of Fountains of Wayne]. I know that his passing affected Josh deeply.

Before taking a break, The Still Out were signed to label Hi-Speed Soul, opened shows for Swervedriver and Longwave, and released a single in honor of Adam. 

Meanwhile, Crystallized track “Let the Listeners Hurt,” featuring guest vocals and guitar from Swervedriver’s Adam Franklin, has been released as a single, and is streaming everywhere now, Listen below. 

Arj also told us more about the song. He said: 

Josh’s infectious bass riff formed the backbone of this song’s demo that was eventually built up with heavy layered guitars. After Josh played the song’s skeleton in a Jersey City bar, Swervedriver’s Adam Franklin happened to hear it and approached him to find out who wrote it. He offered to play on it, and within a few days, Josh and I were in the studio with him rounding out the tune with Adam’s iconic lead guitar and vocals. The result is a loud and taut burst of dynamic intensity, a celebration of movement and vitality.

The reissue was remastered by Greg Calbi and Steve Fallone and includes three bonus tracks: two previously unreleased studio tracks: “Suffocate” and “In Fascination,” and one live performance of “From Fiction” from Arlene’s Grocery in NYC with Mikey from Swervedriver on drums. 

We recently had Adam Franklin of Swervedriver on the BrooklynVegan podcast and he told us this about The Still Out album and their return: 

The album…is a really great album actually…Arjun’s sort of…regrouped the band so that’s going to be awesome….and there’s a single on the album that…I sing and play guitar on…so I think people are going to dig that if they haven’t heard it before because that’s another record that…they seem to take from elements of sort of alternative rock, metal-ly bits, shoegazey bits.

Catch The Still Out supporting Swervedriver on the ‘Raise at 35’ tour at the White Eagle Hall in NJ on August 28 and on August 29 at Music Hall of Williamsburg in Brooklyn.

title: Taking Back Sunday announce ‘Louder Now’ 20th anniversary reissue with bonus 7″ (exclusive vinyl)
content:
One of Taking Back Sunday‘s most classic albums, their 2006 major label debut Louder Now, turns 20 this year, and to celebrate it they’re giving it a new vinyl reissue. The 20th anniversary edition comes with a bonus 7″ featuring two of the album’s B-sides, “Brooklyn (If You See Something, Say Something)” and “Sleep.” We have an exclusive “Amazonite Swirl” vinyl variant of the LP, paired with the 7″ on standard black vinyl, limited to 500 copies and available for pre-order in the BV shop.

Louder Now was TBS’ second consecutive album made with Adam Lazzara on lead vocals, Fred Mascherino on guitar/secondary vocals, Eddie Reyes on guitar, Matt Rubano on bass, and Mark O’Connell on drums, following 2004’s Where You Want to Be. And if Where You Want to Be found the band hanging on to some of the same thrills as their instant-classic debut Tell All Your Friends, Louder Now found this iteration of the band coming into their own, taking a full step forward, and coming out with some of the most iconic songs of TBS’ career, including “MakeDamnSure,” “Liar (It Takes One to Know One),” and “What’s It Feel Like to Be a Ghost?.” Stream it below if you need a refresher, and make (damn) sure to add this to your record collection while it lasts.

Both Mascherino and John Nolan (secondary vocalist/guitarist on Tell All Your Friends and all of their albums from the 2011 self-titled onwards) are part of their current live lineup on tour, which includes fall shows with Thrice and Saves the Day, the latter of whom Adam recently reminisced about driving hours and hours just to see them play back in the day.

One of their upcoming shows, October 14 at the iconic Red Rocks, is a celebration of Louder Now. They also have festival sets on their schedule, and you can see all dates below.

Adam says, “Our record Louder Now represents a huge milestone for me and to know it has made an impact on so many other people’s lives as well is something I still struggle to get my head around. To have the opportunity to celebrate that record with both John Nolan and Fred Mascherino on stage together, along with Shaun Cooper, is incredible to me. The songs sound stronger than I can ever remember live and I can’t even begin to tell you how excited I am to share that with everyone.”

title: Bonnie ‘Prince’ Billy announces live album, shares song ft. Samhain’s London May
content:
Bonnie ‘Prince’ Billy, aka Will Oldham, has announced a new live album that was recorded at The Pico Union Project in Los Angeles over Valentine’s Day weekend 2025, not long after BPB released his great, country-leaning album The Purple Bird. Titled Ghosts of American Psychonauts, the new live album features three songs from that album (“re-arranged with new instrumentation,” according to the announcement), as well as classics like “I See A Darkness” and “Strange Form of Life” and other songs from more recent years.

The first single from the album is a rendition of The Purple Bird‘s “London May,” and it features the actual London May of Samhain on drums. The rendition is a little more haunting than the album version, and very worth hearing. Check it out below.

Ghosts of American Psychonauts was made with Oldham’s touring partners Thomas Deakin (clarinet, down-tuned electric guitar) and Jacob Duncan (flute, saxophone), and, in addition to London May, it features other guests, including Emmett Kelly (bass), Ryder McNair (piano), Dv DeVincentis (sax), Patrick Shiroishi (sax) and The Purple Bird producer Dave Ferguson (who sings on the live album’s rendition of “Downstream”).

Will says:

Everyone on the stage (on this record) knows how to tell stories, musically, and relies on this storytelling to create liveable real spaces. In February of 2025, in Los Angeles, we had stories to share with each other and we did it with a thorough and cathartic push-and-pull with each other, and with the audience.

The sound of the record doesn’t make any sense, nor does its duration, by standard standards, and this allows the record to do what we want music to do which is to make its own sense.

Once you’ve been on the road for years it’s undeniable that the road is also home, because that’s where much of our friends and family are. The stage and the audience were full of friends and family, and music is where we meet.

Bonnie ‘Prince’ Billy will also be very busy on the road throughout the next few months, with tour dates that span from this week through January 2027. That includes a stop at Brooklyn Folk Festival on November 8. All dates are listed below.

BPB also followed The Purple Bird with another new album earlier this year, We Are Together Again.

title: 12 New Songs Out Today
content:
So many artists, so many songs, so little time. Each week we review a handful of new albums (of all genres), round up even more new music that we’d call “indie,” and talk about what metal is coming out. We post music news, track premieres, and more all day. We update a playlist weekly of some of our current favorite tracks. Here’s a daily roundup with a bunch of interesting, newly released songs in one place.

CITIZEN – “GOOD FORTUNE”

Citizen’s anticipated new album Halcyon Blues comes out this week, and ahead of the release, you get to hear its charged-up opening track.

—

WHY? – “IN SPIRIT”

WHY? have announced their ninth album, Oh Golly / Yes Lord, due October 30 via Waterlines. On lead single “In Spirit,” the genre-fluid band lean into rickety, lightly-psychedelic indie rock.

—

NEW RADICALS – “ONE NIGHT ONLY (BREAK LOOSE BREAK FREE!)”

New Radicals have released their first new song since releasing their first and only album-–the one with “You Get What You Give”–28 years ago. It’s for the movie One Night Only and it’s called “One Night Only (Break Loose Break Free!).”

—

LAST DAYS OF HEAVEN – “BLUSHING 1”

Dallas’ shoegazy alt-rockers Last Days of Heaven have released the new track “Blushing 1” via New Morality Zine.

—

CAROLINA OLIVEROS – “OYE CAMINA !”

Combo Chimbita vocalist Carolina Oliveros announced her solo debut, Ya Rompimos el Silencio, due out November 6 via Chulo Records. About new single “Oye Camina,” she says, “‘Oye Camina’ is a reminder that life is constantly in motion and that our challenge is to live with presence, gratitude, and courage before it slips away.”

—

CALIFORNIA COUSINS – PROMO 26

Rochester, NY emo/post-hardcore band California Cousins (aka calicuzns) have dropped a three-song promo and it’s very promising stuff. Hopefully this means we’ll learn more about a new LP sooner than later.

—

LUCY DACUS – “CLAY PIGEONS” & JOHN MORELAND/LYDIA LOVELESS – “FADED LOVES AND MEMORIES” (BLAZE FOLEY COVERS)

Two more tracks are out from the tribute album to the late outlaw country cult hero Blaze Foley, which arrives in full this Friday. Listen to Lucy Dacus’ rendition of “Clay Pigeons” and John Moreland’s rendition of “Faded Loves and Memories” with backing vocals from Lydia Loveless.

—

JAMES ELLIS FORD – “THE EVER AFTER”

“It might seem a little odd to be trying to write dance music from a hospital bed,” says James Ellis Ford of Simian Mobile Disco and producing your favorite band’s latest album, “but I was trying to lift my mood and focus on the positive things in my life. In that moment my mind went to my little 8-year-old boy Frank and the power he has to bring joy into the world and point the way to a better future.” New album Lost In Another World will be out August 14.

—

NO BRA – “18TH FLOOR”

Musician, satirist and provocateur Susanne Oberbeck is back with a new No Bra single. She directed the video, too.

—

BONOBO FT JOY CROOKES – “ALWAYS ON YOUR SIDE”

Here’s another single from Bonobo’s guest-filled Distance and Static that’s out September 11. This one’s with Mercury Prize-nominated singer Joy Crookes.

—

NOW IT’S OVERHEAD – “ELEVEN-SEVEN-THIRTY-FIVE”

Now It’s Overhead are back with their first new music in 20 years. “eleven-seven-thirty-five” is from their new EP, which is out in September via Saddle Creek, and you can read more about it here.

—
